AttributeError: module 'rti.rpc' has no.cause: The class is called Requester, not Client.
AttributeError: module 'rti.rpc' has no.fix: Use `from rti.rpc import Requester` and create `Requester(request_type=..., reply_type=..., participant=..., service_name=...)`

AttributeError: 'Requester' object has n.cause: There is no is_service_available() method. Use the matched_replier_count property instead.
AttributeError: 'Requester' object has n.fix: Poll `requester.matched_replier_count > 0` in a loop with small sleep intervals.

AttributeError: 'Requester' object has n.cause: The method is called receive_replies, not wait_for_replies.
The method is called receive_replies, not take_replies.

idl.dataclass is not defined.cause: There is no @idl.dataclass decorator. Use @idl.struct instead.
idl.dataclass is not defined.fix: Replace @idl.dataclass with @idl.struct. Use member_annotations for bounded strings.

idl.StringType is not defined.cause: String bounds are specified via member_annotations, not StringType.

idl.int32 is not defined.cause: Use native Python int type, not idl.int32.
idl.int32 is not defined.fix: Replace `idl.int32` with `int` in your @idl.struct class fields.

Late joiner receives 0 or 1 samples inst.cause: Missing one or more of: TRANSIENT_LOCAL durability, RELIABLE reliability, or KEEP_ALL history. Default KEEP_LAST depth=1 only stores the latest sample.
Late joiner receives 0 or 1 samples inst.fix: Set ALL THREE on both writer and reader: durability=TRANSIENT_LOCAL, reliability=RELIABLE, history=KEEP_ALL. Also use writer.wait_for_acknowledgments() instead of time.sleep().

Subscriber misses data when starting aft.cause: VOLATILE durability means the writer does not cache samples for late joiners.
Subscriber misses data when starting aft.fix: Change durability to TRANSIENT_LOCAL on both writer and reader. Also set RELIABLE reliability and KEEP_ALL history.

publisher_guid field is empty or missing.cause: GUID extraction from publication_handle requires a two-step process.
publisher_guid field is empty or missing.fix:
1) Get handle: pub_handle = sample.info.publication_handle
2) Look up data: pub_data = reader.matched_publication_data(pub_handle)
3) Format GUID: format_guid(pub_data.key) using struct.pack on the key.value tuple

AttributeError: 'Subscriber' object has.cause: Built-in topic readers are accessed from the participant, not the subscriber.
AttributeError: 'Subscriber' object has.fix: Use participant.subscription_reader for DCPSSubscription built-in topic.

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rt.cause: RTI Connext DDS Python bindings are installed in the project's virtual environment, NOT in the system Python. System Python (3.14) does not have rti.connextdds.
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rt.fix: Use the virtual environment Python: run `which python3.10` or `which python3.12` to find an RTI-enabled Python. The project .venv/bin/python has RTI installed. Do NOT try `pip install rti.connextdds` — it is a commercial product and is not on PyPI.

UnsupportedError: Can't create an AnyDat.cause: Built-in topic DataReaders cannot be wrapped in AnyDataReader. Access them directly from the participant.
UnsupportedError: Can't create an AnyDat.fix: Use `participant.builtin_subscriber` to get the built-in subscriber, then access publication/subscription readers directly. For publication data: iterate `dds.PublicationBuiltinTopicData.DataReader.find_by_topic(participant, 'DCPSPublication')` or use `participant.publication_reader`.

Guid constructor: TypeError or Attribute.cause: DDS GUIDs are not constructed directly. They are extracted from BuiltinTopicKey values on discovery data.
Guid constructor: TypeError or Attribute.fix: Get GUID from matched_publication_data(handle).key.value — this returns a tuple of 4 uint32. Format with struct.pack('>I', v) for each value, then format as 'xx.xx.xx.xx.xx.xx.xx.xx.xx.xx.xx.xx|x.x.x.xx'.

TypeError: 'rti.connextdds.Guid' object.cause: dds.Guid is a type, not a callable constructor. You cannot create GUID objects directly. GUIDs are extracted from discovery data.
TypeError: 'rti.connextdds.Guid' object.fix: Do NOT call dds.Guid(). Instead: 1) Get pub_data = reader.matched_publication_data(sample.info.publication_handle), 2) Access pub_data.key.value (tuple of 4 uint32), 3) Format with struct.pack('>I', v) for each value. Use the get_pattern('guid_formatting') tool for the complete pattern.

wait_for_service returned False or timed.cause: wait_for_service() is unreliable in RTI Python RPC. It may return False even when the service is available.
wait_for_service returned False or timed.fix: Use matched_replier_count polling instead: `while requester.matched_replier_count == 0: time.sleep(0.1)` with a timeout. This directly checks DDS discovery.

Publisher exits before late joiner recei.cause: Publisher needs to stay alive long enough for TRANSIENT_LOCAL cache to be delivered to late-joining readers.
Publisher exits before late joiner recei.fix: After publishing all samples, use `time.sleep(5)` to keep the process alive. This is simpler and more reliable than wait_for_acknowledgments, which raises TimeoutError when no readers have matched yet.

@idl.struct subscriber receives 0 sample.cause: CRITICAL TYPE INCOMPATIBILITY: When a publisher uses DynamicData, an @idl.struct subscriber will receive ZERO samples. The two type representations are incompatible at the DDS middleware level, even if the fields match.
@idl.struct subscriber receives 0 sample.fix: Use DynamicData.DataReader instead of @idl.struct. Steps: 1) topic = dds.DynamicData.Topic.find(participant, 'TopicName'), 2) reader = dds.DynamicData.DataReader(participant.implicit_subscriber, topic), 3) Access fields with bracket notation: sample.data['field_name']. Use get_pattern('dynamicdata_subscriber') for the complete pattern.

AttributeError: type object 'rti.connext.cause: find_by_topic is NOT on the generic DataReader class. It is a class method on specific typed DataReader classes like PublicationBuiltinTopicData.DataReader or SubscriptionBuiltinTopicData.DataReader.
AttributeError: type object 'rti.connext.fix: For builtin topics use: dds.PublicationBuiltinTopicData.DataReader.find_by_topic(participant.builtin_subscriber, 'DCPSPublication'). For regular data topics, create a DynamicData.DataReader: first create a StructType, then dds.DynamicData.Topic(), then dds.DynamicData.DataReader(). See get_pattern('dynamicdata_subscriber').

Subscriber receives no data despite corr.cause: Type mismatch between publisher and subscriber. If the publisher uses DynamicData and the subscriber uses @idl.struct (or vice versa), zero samples will be delivered. This is the most common cause of 'no data received' when QoS is correct.
Subscriber receives no data despite corr.fix: Use DynamicData.Topic.find() to discover the topic, then create a DynamicData.DataReader. This automatically matches the publisher's type representation. See get_pattern('dynamicdata_subscriber').
